title.narrative: Annual Output Results
Output Indicator

description.narrative:
1. International and local observers rate the conduct of elections as free, fair, transparent, participatory and inclusive.
2. The ability of NEC and elections stakeholders to cooperate and work together for the conduct of credible elections 3. Elections are conducted under peaceful atmosphere and the rule of laws is used as remedial action for redress.

comment.narrative: Electoral support for the 2015-2018 election cycle, in the form of technical assistance ended early 2020. During the period of implementation, the project was focused on strengthening both human and institutional capacities of NEC to enable the Commission implements its statutory mandates in an impartial and credible manner. There has been gains made so far in achieving this objective but the need for continuous support, amidst prevailing economic conditions facing the country coupled with the need to sustain democratic gains and the Country fragile peace, are necessitating factors that gave rise to further implementation of the 2020-2024 -Liberia Electoral Support Project.

1. CSOs or FBOs hired to conduct civic and voter outreach programs across the 73 electoral districts 2. At least 10 engagement activities targeting women and PWDs in place 3. At least 50% of CVE messages available in local languages. 4. At lease 4 seminars and trainings carried out with a focus on equipping civil society organizations, and other electoral stakeholders 5.100% of the electoral staff trained before elections 6. Two security booths at Nec HQ renovated. 7. 5,000 updated Elections security Booklets are printed and distributed to LNP ahead of 2020 elections 8 . At least 70 percent of project interlocutors understand impact of electoral violence on women

1. Public knowledge on electoral processes increased with sensitization and awareness on electoral conflict prevention, all contributing to peaceful conduct of the 2020 SSE and Referendum. 2. The 2020 elections and referendum was Inclusive and participatory thus promoting public trust and confidence in the elections management body. This was as a result of continuous stakeholders engagements before and after the elections. 3. Confident levels of elections staff were improved through capacity building trainings, thus contributing to a successful conduct of the elections. 4. Elections security was strengthened through capacity building of national security personnel, thus preventing and in some instances arresting potential threats of electoral violence including violence against women across the Country.

1. Communication policy framework and strategy for NEC updated and approved by the NEC BoC 2. Misinformation platform developed and used by electoral stakeholders 3. Capacity assessment of NEC and Electoral Stakeholders conducted in 2021. 4. All NEC departments use ERP online platform for work processes (enterprise Resource Planning system) 5. At least one Feasibility study for bio-metric voter registration conducted 6. One Need assessment for additional electoral support to peace building and conflict resolution conducted.

Communication policy and strategic place done and submitted to the Board of commissioner of NEC for adoption. Six out of 10 engagement activities targeting women and PWDs were conducted, resulting in the revision and of an MoU on increased women political participation. Additionally, a draft policy on inclusion of persons living with disabilities into the electoral processes as voters and candidates. feasibility study conducted on a possible introduction of bio-metric voter registration system in Liberia, with actionable recommendation for electoral stakeholders consideration. Representatives of political parties received knowledge on VAWIE, thereby instituting programs and measures to address issues of electoral violence against women.
Assessment of technical and operational capacities of the Early Warning and Early Response Mechanism (EWER),was conducted, leading to the approval of assistance to peace building and conflict prevention through the Peace Building Office. In view of said support, a situation room intended to track issue of violence especially electoral violence has be established and furnished with support from the project.
One CVE cell consultation workshop was successfully conducted for the establishment of CVE cell in electoral districts.

1. Early warning and response mechanisms supported to promote conflict prevention and prevention of VAWIE. 2. Conduct One round-table meeting with lawmakers and party executives on VAWIE 3. Two Discussions or dialogue forum on VAWIE held at universities and high schools with former and aspirant candidates and politicians. 4 Conduct at least four of round tables with Political parties hierarchy, women & youth wings, COPWIL from 15 counties to ensure adherence to Article 4.5 Elections Law and develop Action plan for 2023 election) 5. Revitalize Gender Election Coordination Group (GECG) in fifteen counties to be– linked to CVE cells (Four regional workshops to be conducted). 6. Conduct one BRIDGE TTF for NEC departments and key representatives of electoral stakeholders to enhance capacity in conducting regular staff trainings 7.Conduct at least one BRIDGE Training for members of the Board of Commissioners of NEC 8. NEC public perception improved by at least 60% 9. Consolidated and sustainable Early Warning Mechanism platform designed based on existing structures
